title: Critère de platitude par fibres
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$, $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$, $(S',\mathfrak m_{S'})$ be local rings and $R\xrightarrow{\alpha}S\xrightarrow{\beta}S'$ local homomorphisms ($\alpha(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, $\beta(\mathfrak m_S)\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S'}$); let $M$ be an $S'$-module, regarded as an $S$-module and an $R$-module by restriction of scalars. Assume (1) $S$ and $S'$ are essentially of finite presentation over $R$: each is isomorphic, as an $R$-algebra (via $\alpha$, resp. $\beta\circ\alpha$), to a localization $W^{-1}B$ of a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] at a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq B$; (2) $M$ is an $S'$-module of finite presentation ($M\cong\operatorname{coker}(S'^{\oplus a}\to S'^{\oplus b})$ for some $a,b\ge0$ and some $S'$-linear map); (3) $M\neq0$; (4) $M/\mathfrak m_RM$ is a flat module over $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; (5) $M$ is a flat $R$-module. Then $S$ is flat over $R$ and $M$ is a flat $S$-module.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-flat-closed-fiber-model] to obtain $R_0,S_0,T_0,N_0$, finite $N_0$, its base and fibre flatness, and the two localized base-change comparisons. This groups the original limit-system argument; it stops before the Noetherian fibre criterion.

The module $N_0$ is nonzero. If it were zero then $S\otimes_{S_0}N_0$, and its module localization, would be zero. Its $S$-linear isomorphism with $M$ contradicts $M\ne0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian] to obtain $S_0$ flat over $R_0$ and $N_0$ flat over $S_0$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change], $R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$ is flat over $R$ and $S\otimes_{S_0}N_0$ is flat over $S$. Apply [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness] to these modules and their respective multiplicative subsets. Transport flatness across the supplied $R$- and $S$-linear isomorphisms (Mathlib Module.Flat.equiv_iff). This gives both conclusions.
